TetraHashGridEncode supports multi-resolution encoding which can be used in conjunction with progressive training strategies.
Choose Progressive Training when starting with low-resolution details and gradually adding complexity.
-   **Time Complexity:** The forward pass is $O(N \times L)$, where $N$ is the number of points and $L$ is the number of levels.
Each point requires constant-time operations (hashing, interpolation) per level.
-   **Memory Complexity:** The memory usage is dominated by the feature table, which is $O(L \times \text{table\_size} \times F)$.
Hash collisions can occur, though the large table size mitigates this.
-   **When to use:** When training NeRFs or SDFs on consumer GPUs with limited memory, and when tetrahedral interpolation is desired for its gradient properties.
-   **When not to use:** When CPU-only inference is required, or when adaptive resolution is critical for the scene structure.
TetraHashGridEncode was introduced as part of the TetraSDF project by NAVER Corp.
It is designed to provide a differentiable encoding method that combines the efficiency of hash grids with the geometric properties of tetrahedral decomposition.
